skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At the outset the interviewer said 'I represent the company, not you' and identified the Special Committee, but never said counsel cannot give the witness legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains the privilege belongs to the company and the company may decide to share what is said.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: No ground rules on speculation, estimates or clarification and no invitation to separate recollection from uncertainty; the interviewer went straight to questions.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 ends 'Any questions?' and the witness answers 'No. Go ahead.' but understanding of the warning was never checked.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T80 asks if there is anything else the Committee should know, and T86 gives a confidentiality reminder and asks for documents to be kept; no next steps were given.

moments.text: I represent the company, not you. What we discuss is privileged, but the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell me. Any questions?
No. Go ahead.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep any related documents and keep this confidential.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Some open prompts work well (T10, T16, T40), but most questions are short and closed, so the witness is rarely allowed to walk through events uninterrupted.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moves from role (T4) to staff (T6-T9) to LJM1 (T10) to specific transactions and documents later in the interview.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Several compound or leading questions, e.g. T22 'Who negotiated it on both sides, and did anyone object?' and T68 'You negotiated the Chewco buyout yourself, didn't you?'

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Remains polite and in control throughout, even when confronting the witness with inconsistencies at T58 and T72.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Changes direction after answers: T34 after the Skilling claim, T40 asks for a specific deal, T50 pushes a vague answer, and T58 and T72 respond to documents.

moments.text: Moves from general role questions to people, Kopper, LJM1 and the Board, a sensible general-to-specific order.
Tell me about the June 28, 1999 Board meeting. What did you present?
Chewco was formed in 1997 to buy CalPERS' interest in JEDI, wasn't it?
How did those reviews work in practice? Take a specific deal.
Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?
Why didn't you tell the Board?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Several evasions went unchallenged: T43 approvals papered after closing, T67 deflecting withheld LJM2 returns, and T73 'I don't recall receiving it' after the memo was shown.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Asks who (T32, T60), when (T42), what (T30) and how (T38), though the timing and mechanics of the $2.6M payment were not fully pinned down.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Used the Southampton agreement (T58) and the memo (T72) to refresh, but did not use the approval sheets when the witness said he would have to look at them (T43) or pursue the Foundation's records (T55).

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: T34-T35 separates Skilling's Board disclosure as hearsay ('I don't know that personally') and T38-T39 separates what he assumed from what he checked.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T82 asks who else to speak with and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T84 asks about documents, and the witness names approval sheets, Board materials and partnership agreements; the interviewer then used the Southampton agreement.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Repeatedly asks how the witness knows things (T34, T38), when approvals were signed (T42) and how far returns were above 30% (T50).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Followed up well on Southampton, Chewco and the memo, but five key leads (T31, T43, T59, T65, T67) were never followed up, so the cap applies.

skills.name: Effective Selection

skills.reason: Documents were relevant and used, but authentication was thin: T58 says only 'This is the Southampton Place partnership agreement' and T72 does not establish the memo's source.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Obtained the witness's account first (T52-T57 before the Southampton agreement; T70-T71 before the memo).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: T58 describes the $25,000 contribution and $4.5 million receipt accurately, and T72 states the $10.5 million figure correctly, though the description is brief.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.

moments.text: I represent the company, not you. What we discuss is privileged, but the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell me. Any questions?
No. Go ahead.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep any related documents and keep this confidential.
Opened with role questions, then Global Finance, then LJM1, moving from general to specific.
Take a specific deal.
What controls applied to LJM2, and did they actually work?
Chewco was formed in 1997 to buy CalPERS' interest in JEDI, wasn't it?
You negotiated the Chewco buyout yourself, didn't you?
Approximately, then.

area_evidence.area: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

moments.text: What were those considerations?
How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.
I assumed it was followed. I didn't check each one myself.
Some approvals were papered after a deal closed. That happened.
I'd want to see the investor reports before giving a number.
It may have. It was a small amount.
I don't recall receiving it. Michael kept me informed about things generally. Being informed isn't the same as negotiating.
I don't recall authorizing it.
I may have had a call with them about it. I don't remember the details.
Asked who else to speak with; witness named Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E.
The deal files are at the company: the approval sheets, the Board and Finance Committee materials, and the partnership agreements.
Did you personally have any financial interest in the Rhythms unwind?

This is the Southampton Place partnership agreement. It shows a $25,000 contribution from your family foundation, and our information is the foundation received about $4.5 million about six weeks later. Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?
The Foundation isn't me, and what I told the Board was about my economics as general partner.
This note to "Andy" mentions $10.5 million for the buyout. So you were involved, weren't you?

missed_chances.description: Witness admitted some approvals were papered after closing; interviewer moved on without asking which deals or who knew.
missed_chances.question: Which LJM2 approvals were signed after closing, and who knew when Causey and Buy signed?

missed_chances.description: Witness said he may have called in-house counsel about the $2.6M payment; interviewer moved on without following up.
missed_chances.question: What did in-house counsel tell you on that call, and did you tell anyone the payment should be made?

tips: Before we begin, do you understand that I represent the Company, cannot give you legal advice, and that you may wish to consult your own counsel?
Walk me through the $2.6M tax indemnity request step by step: who asked for it, what counsel said, who you spoke with, and what you decided?
